topStories.headline: KEXP Music Hub Planned for Haight and Ashbury Corner — But Six Small Businesses Could Lose Their Storefronts
topStories.dek: SF Heritage has selected Seattle radio nonprofit KEXP and the Blue Bear School of Music to transform the historic Doolan-Larson Building into a broadcast studio, music school, and rooftop concert venue — a plan that has alarmed the merchants currently occupying its ground floor.
topStories.body:
San Francisco Heritage has chosen KEXP, the Seattle-based nonprofit public radio station, and the Blue Bear School of Music as partners to reimagine the historic Doolan-Larson Building at the corner of Haight and Ashbury streets into a music and cultural hub. The announcement, first reported by the San Francisco Chronicle on September 17 and confirmed by multiple outlets, envisions a broadcast studio for Bay Area radio programming, a full floor of music classrooms for Blue Bear, a flexible street-level gathering space, and a rooftop venue capable of hosting around 100 people for concerts, DJ nights, and open mics.

The Doolan-Larson Building was constructed in 1903 and rebuilt after the 1906 earthquake. SF Heritage has stewarded it since 2017, when longtime owner Norm Larson donated the landmark to the nonprofit. Three teams submitted proposals in June 2026; KEXP's plan was selected as the sole finalist in August. The organizations say they will spend the coming months determining whether the project is feasible, with a first substantive update expected in early 2027. KEXP needs to raise more than $16 million for construction, and the project still requires SF Planning approval and must satisfy the building's historic protections.

The proposal has drawn immediate opposition from the six small businesses currently renting the ground-floor storefronts. Merchants told the SF Standard they face displacement if the plan moves forward; at least one retailer made protest banners and T-shirts reading "Heritage Should Preserve Community Not Displace It." SF Heritage, for its part, describes the project as an active neighborhood cultural hub rather than a museum piece — one intended to preserve the historic character of the property while opening it to public use.

Neighborhood opinion is divided. Supporters see the hub as a fitting tribute to a corner synonymous with the counterculture and a way to activate a landmark that has never fully lived up to its significance. Critics argue that replacing working neighborhood businesses with an institution backed by outside money repeats the displacement story that has reshaped the Haight for decades. No construction timeline has been set and the project remains in an exploratory phase.

topStories.headline: HANC Meets Tonight to Dissect 'Fatal Flaws' in Lurie's Citywide Rezoning Plan
topStories.dek: The Haight Ashbury Neighborhood Council's October general meeting focuses on Mayor Lurie's upzoning proposal — which passed the Planning Commission 4–3 in September and now heads to the Board of Supervisors — and on charter reform ballot measures ahead of the November 3 election.
topStories.body:
The Haight Ashbury Neighborhood Council holds its October general membership meeting tonight, Thursday October 9, at 7:00 p.m. in a hybrid format. The session is devoted to Mayor Lurie's sweeping rezoning proposal — what HANC describes as the largest city-initiated rezoning in San Francisco in 50 years, covering the entire Haight-Ashbury and most of western and central San Francisco.

HANC has identified five core objections to the plan: that it would incentivize demolition of rent-controlled units and displace thousands of current residents; that it would eliminate neighborhood-serving businesses and nonprofits from targeted retail streets; that it removes density controls without meaningful affordability requirements for new market-rate housing; that it strips public participation from the approval process; and that it repeals affordable housing and transit impact fee requirements. At a Planning Commission hearing on September 11, the measure passed 4–3, with no supervisor-appointed commissioner voting yes — a split HANC has characterized as evidence of the proposal's partisan character.

The political arithmetic at the Board of Supervisors has shifted in recent weeks. The recall of District 7 Supervisor Matt Engardio — linked in part to his support for the rezoning — means Mayor Lurie must appoint a replacement vote. At least four supervisors currently oppose the existing plan. A Land Use Committee hearing is scheduled for October 20 at City Hall, Room 250. Final votes before the full Board are not expected until December or January.

Also on tonight's agenda: the November 3 election, for which HANC has published endorsements on its website including positions on Lurie's three charter reform ballot measures — Propositions A, E, and F — all of which the council recommends voters reject. A citywide coalition called Neighbors United, of which HANC is a member, has filed a letter outlining legal objections to the rezoning and is discussing a ballot challenge for the June 2027 ballot. Participation details for the hybrid meeting are at hanc-sf.org.

topStories.headline: SF Demands State Probe of 40 PG&E Blackouts — Haight-Ashbury Among the Hardest Hit Neighborhoods
topStories.dek: City leaders sent a letter to state regulators this week documenting 40 large-scale PG&E outages since December, including a March blackout that cut power to 14,000 customers from the Castro to Haight-Ashbury and a Golden Gate Park-area outage as recently as October 6.
topStories.body:
San Francisco city leaders filed a letter with the California Public Utilities Commission on October 8 demanding a state investigation into PG&E's reliability record. According to the letter, there have been 40 large-scale blackouts — each affecting more than 1,000 customers — since the December 20 disaster that darkened roughly one-third of the city, a pace of nearly one outage per week.

The Haight-Ashbury and surrounding neighborhoods have been repeatedly affected. A March 20 rolling blackout struck from the Castro to Haight-Ashbury, cutting power to 14,000 customers, according to the city's letter. An August 29 outage knocked out electricity for more than 6,000 customers in Haight-Ashbury, the Western Addition, and adjacent areas — repair crews restored most service by 9:15 a.m. but full power did not return until early afternoon. As recently as Tuesday, October 6, a large unplanned outage hit the area around Golden Gate Park, affecting more than 4,400 customers.

The city's letter to the CPUC also highlights two PG&E underground electrical vault fires in downtown San Francisco on September 17 and October 1, and four city infrastructure projects undertaken by PG&E that have hit major delays. City leaders have criticized PG&E for its intention to sell a deactivated substation located one block from the one that failed in December. State Senator Scott Wiener introduced Senate Bill 875 earlier this year to reform eminent domain procedures and make it easier for San Francisco to acquire PG&E's local distribution grid.

Residents and small businesses that suffered losses in any of the outages are encouraged to document damages and contact PG&E directly about compensation. The full CPUC letter is referenced in the SF Standard's October 8 report.

moreNews.headline: Pasta Supply Co. Targeting October Opening at 919 Cole St. in Cole Valley
moreNews.body: Chef Anthony Strong announced in August 2026 that Pasta Supply Co. — his popular fresh-pasta shop and restaurant — will open a third San Francisco location at 919 Cole Street, the former Peet's Coffee space in Cole Valley, with an October target date. The roughly 700-square-foot counter-service spot will seat about 24 diners and serve lunch and dinner daily, offering 30 fresh pasta shapes along with sauces and cooking staples for takeout. Strong, who has lived in Cole Valley for 12 years, is crowdfunding the $400,000 buildout directly through the restaurant, offering one-year ($550) and lifetime ($4,000) pasta subscriptions as rewards. As of late August, the campaign was already halfway to its goal one week in.

moreNews.headline: HANC Board Nominations Open Through November Meeting
moreNews.body: The Haight Ashbury Neighborhood Council announced on October 4 that nominations for its board are open through the November membership meeting. All current HANC members are eligible to nominate; those who have been members for at least three months are eligible to serve. The new term runs from December 2026 through November 2027. Nominations can be submitted at the October 9 meeting or before the vote at the November meeting.

restaurants.name: Parada 22

restaurants.name: Magnolia Brewing – Haight
restaurants.description: Haight Street's landmark craft brewery and gastropub, reopened in late 2024 under new local ownership with a refreshed taproom, house-brewed beers, and elevated pub food.

restaurants.name: The Alembic

restaurants.name: Pork Store Cafe
restaurants.description: Much-loved Haight Street diner serving enormous portions of scratch-made breakfast and brunch at affordable prices since 1989.

restaurants.name: Escape From New York Pizza

restaurants.description: One of the Haight's most storied dive bars, with Persian-themed décor, a circular bar, and perfectly made martinis in a setting unchanged for decades.

restaurants.name: Zazie
restaurants.description: Beloved Cole Valley French bistro open since 1992, famous for its weekend brunch with Provençal-inspired eggs, crêpes, and a sunny back patio.

restaurants.name: Beit Rima
restaurants.description: Award-winning Cole Valley spot serving Arabic comfort food — hand-kneaded bread, crispy falafel, chicken skewers, and za'atar-dusted pita — with a devoted neighborhood following.

restaurants.name: Cole Valley Tavern
restaurants.description: Neighborhood go-to American bar with a warm dining room, rotating food specials, and an ice cream window that draws lines on warm evenings.

restaurants.name: InoVino
restaurants.description: Intimate Cole Valley wine bar with an excellent selection of Italian bottles, solid pastas, and charcuterie-and-cheese boards in a cozy setting.

restaurants.name: Crepes On Cole
restaurants.description: Casual Cole Valley standby open late most nights, offering sweet and savory crêpes, burgers, and beer in a relaxed neighbourhood setting.

restaurants.name: Toronado
restaurants.description: Lower Haight craft-beer pilgrimage site with 50 taps of rare and sought-after brews, sticker-plastered walls, and a cash-only, no-nonsense vibe — now under new local ownership as of June 2026.

restaurants.name: Bar Jabroni
restaurants.description: Lively Lower Haight wine bar pouring chilled reds and orange wines alongside small plates like beef tartare with Szechuan peppercorns and house-made focaccia.

restaurants.name: Nopalito
restaurants.description: Organic, from-scratch Mexican cooking from the Nopa team, plating blue-corn tacos, carnitas, and mole made with local and sustainable ingredients.

restaurants.name: Noc Noc
restaurants.description: Lower Haight bar with trippy, Tim Burton-esque décor that is a neighbourhood fixture — only in San Francisco.

restaurants.name: Danny Coyle's
restaurants.description: Friendly Lower Haight Irish bar open until 2am, with a great tap selection, sports on TV, and a loyal neighbourhood crowd.

restaurants.name: Woods Lowside
restaurants.description: Casual Lower Haight bar with crisp, dry house beers, natural wines, Detroit-style pizza from Joyride Pizza on site, and a heated back patio.

restaurants.name: Bambino's Ristorante
restaurants.description: Charming old-school Italian restaurant in Cole Valley with hearty classic pastas and a warm, neighbourhood trattoria feel.

restaurants.name: Double Black
restaurants.description: New Cole Valley coffee shop inside the Yardsale outdoor apparel store, drawing queues for iced hojicha lattes with black-sesame cold foam.

hotels.name: Stanyan Park Hotel
hotels.description: Listed on the National Register of Historic Places, this 1904 Beaux Arts Victorian hotel sits across from Golden Gate Park and includes a daily continental breakfast and weekday wine-and-cheese reception.

hotels.name: The Metro Hotel
hotels.description: Family-owned 23-room boutique hotel on Divisadero with original artwork throughout, a private garden, and a welcoming eco-conscious ethos steps from Haight-Ashbury.

shops.name: Booksmith
shops.description: Haight Street's landmark independent bookstore since 1976, offering a wide selection of new titles and hosting more than 200 author events per year.

shops.name: Amoeba Music
shops.description: Enormous independent music store claiming the world's largest selection of new and used vinyl, CDs, DVDs, and posters — a pilgrimage site for music fans since 1990.

shops.name: Love on Haight
shops.description: SF Legacy Business since 1989 selling vibrant tie-dye clothing and accessories by more than 175 local and international artists, keeping the Haight's countercultural spirit alive.

shops.name: Wasteland
shops.description: Glamorous Haight Street vintage and resale boutique with a carefully curated mix of high-end secondhand fashion and designer pieces — buy, sell, or trade.

shops.name: Piedmont Boutique
shops.description: An unofficial Haight landmark identifiable by the giant fishnet-stocking legs hanging from the second-floor window, selling costumes, festival wear, and dramatic accessories.

shops.name: Relic Vintage
shops.description: Go-to Haight Street vintage shop since 2012, housing carefully selected garments from the 1920s through the 1980s and a strong collection of statement accessories.

shops.name: Say Cheese
shops.description: Cole Valley institution since 1976 offering an extensive world cheese selection alongside charcuterie, wines, olives, artisanal snacks, and loaded deli sandwiches.

shops.name: San Francisco Mercantile
shops.description: Haight Street retail shop partnered with San Francisco Heritage, selling locally made gifts, detailed neighborhood maps, art, and keepsakes by Bay Area artists.

shops.name: Woot Bear
shops.type: Designer toy store and art gallery
shops.description: Haight Street collectible toy boutique and gallery hosting monthly art shows alongside a floor-to-ceiling selection of designer figures from Tokidoki, Pop Mart, Kidrobot, and more.

shops.name: Pipe Dreams
shops.description: SF Legacy Business at 1376 Haight Street and a touchstone of the neighbourhood's countercultural roots since the 1960s.

shops.name: Cole Hardware
shops.type: Independent hardware and home goods store
shops.description: Beloved Cole Valley institution and local alternative to big-box hardware stores, stocking household essentials, plants, and an eclectic range of gifts.

artEntertainment.name: The DeLuxe
artEntertainment.description: Beloved Haight Street jazz venue reborn in June 2026 after a three-year closure: restored Art Deco interior, rebuilt stage, upgraded sound, craft cocktails, and live music seven nights a week.

artEntertainment.name: Haight Street Art Center
artEntertainment.type: Non-profit poster art gallery and printmaking studio
artEntertainment.description: Non-profit gallery and printmaking studio in Lower Haight dedicated to the history and culture of poster art, with free rotating exhibitions open Thursday through Sunday noon–6pm.

artEntertainment.name: Woot Bear Gallery
artEntertainment.type: Designer toy and contemporary art gallery
artEntertainment.description: Monthly rotating art exhibitions alongside a curated selection of collectible designer toys, featuring artists from around the world in a compact Haight Street space.

artEntertainment.name: Amoeba Music (Live Events)

artEntertainment.description: The Haight Street record store regularly hosts free in-store performances and release events across genres, making it a casual live-music destination in its own right.

artEntertainment.name: Kezar Stadium
artEntertainment.description: Century-old stadium in the southeast corner of Golden Gate Park, the original home of the San Francisco 49ers, now hosting amateur sports leagues, track workouts, high school events, and FC City matches.

gymsRecreation.name: HAUM Studios – Haight-Ashbury
gymsRecreation.description: Award-winning, LGBTQ+-owned yoga studio at Stanyan Street offering Vinyasa, Hatha, Slow Flow, Restorative Yoga, soundbaths, and breathwork classes for all levels, seven days a week.

gymsRecreation.name: Folk Yoga
gymsRecreation.description: Community-centred yoga and fitness studio on Divisadero offering a wide range of class styles including Flow, Restore, and prenatal yoga with highly rated instructors.

gymsRecreation.name: Kezar Pavilion

gymsRecreation.name: Golden Gate Park Panhandle

gymsRecreation.name: Buena Vista Park
gymsRecreation.description: San Francisco's oldest public park, offering wooded trails, sweeping city views, and a popular off-leash dog area on a forested hill above Haight-Ashbury.
